evals.prompt: I built a churn model for our SaaS customers with XGBoost and got 0.97 AUC on a random 80/20 split. Features include tenure, logins_30d, support_tickets, plan, last_invoice_status and account_manager_notes_len. My VP wants to roll it out next week to drive retention offers. Can you help me write up the results for her?
evals.expected_output: Does NOT just write the write-up. Flags 0.97 AUC as a leakage red flag, questions last_invoice_status / notes timing, recommends a temporal split with a label-window gap, a baseline, threshold chosen from offer cost/capacity, and only then a BLUF summary with caveats.
assertions: Flags the 0.97 AUC as likely leakage and does not produce a rollout-ready write-up
Names last_invoice_status and account_manager_notes_len as leak suspects and explains the timing mechanism
States that features must be rebuilt as-of the prediction date (a temporal split alone does not fix overwritten/post-outcome features)
Recommends a temporal (out-of-time) validation with a gap, not only 'use a time split'
Includes a baseline comparison (current rule and/or simple model) in the proposed validation, and the provided script actually implements it
Recommends a randomized no-offer holdout/pilot to measure whether retention offers actually work
Ties the model to the decision: threshold from contact capacity or offer cost vs saved-customer value
Any validation script provided runs and detects a planted post-outcome leak (grader verifies on synthetic data)
The reply to the user fits roughly one page with depth in attachments, and references no files/scripts that are not included
Numbers and recommendations are consistent across the reply and any memo

evals.prompt: we ran a checkout test for 9 days. control 48,210 users 2,031 orders, treatment 50,944 users 2,260 orders. PM says treatment won by 5% and wants to ship. is that right?
evals.expected_output: Runs SRM first (this split fails SRM, p << 0.001), says results can't be trusted until assignment is debugged; notes 9 days isn't full two weekly cycles; shows what the lift/CI would be but frames it as not decision-grade.
assertions: Detects sample ratio mismatch (p << 0.001) and says results are not trustworthy until assignment/logging is fixed
Conversion rates and relative lift computed correctly (~4.21% vs ~4.44%, ~+5.3%)
Reports uncertainty (CI and/or p ~0.08) and notes the lift is not statistically detectable even ignoring SRM
Quantifies or reasons concretely about how the SRM could bias the lift (direction/size depends on who the missing/extra users are)
Raises test-duration issues (9 days < two weekly cycles) and/or peeking / pre-registration
Mentions guardrail metrics (e.g., revenue per user, AOV, errors) before shipping
Gives concrete next steps including debugging assignment and an A/A test or verified rerun with a pre-set sample size
Recommendations and numbers are internally consistent (e.g., rerun duration stated the same everywhere)
Concise: the core answer is readable in under a page

evals.prompt: Our marketing team launched a loyalty program in Texas and Florida in March 2026 but not other states. They want to know how much incremental revenue per customer it caused. I have monthly revenue by state from 2024 through August 2026 in Snowflake. How should I approach this?
evals.expected_output: Recommends DiD or synthetic control, states the parallel-trends assumption, pre-trend/event-study and placebo checks, clustered SEs by state, few-treated-units caveat, language ladder for the claim, and a reconciliation step against finance revenue.
assertions: Recommends DiD and/or synthetic control with a clear primary estimator
Handles differential seasonality between TX/FL and controls (e.g., YoY differencing, state-by-month effects) and explains why
Addresses inference with only 2 treated units (permutation/placebo inference; not relying on clustered SEs)
Proposes pre-trend/event-study and placebo date/state falsification checks
Defines a 'per customer' denominator that the program itself cannot change (e.g., fixed pre-launch customer base) and discusses composition effects
Distinguishes effect per customer in state vs per enrolled member
Includes a false-positive check (no-effect simulation) or power discussion given 2 treated states
Recommends pre-registering the analysis plan and/or reconciling revenue to finance
Any provided script runs and its claimed simulation results reproduce (grader verifies)
Causal language hedged appropriately; reply concise with depth in attachments

evals.prompt: Here's my fraud model repo (train.py, features.py, evaluate.py, data/ with train/valid/holdout parquet). Current PR-AUC is 0.31. Go into experiment mode and push it as high as you can overnight — latency must stay under 30ms. Don't wait for me.
evals.expected_output: Drafts the charter, measures seed noise, runs labbook init with evaluate.py and holdout locked plus a latency guardrail, and loops atomic commit/run/log/revert without asking for anything the charter covers. Prioritizes features and data over hyperparameters, handles plateaus, runs a confirmation re-run and a single holdout score, and ends with a report.
assertions: Writes an explicit plan/charter before iterating (metric, budget, guardrail, locked files)
evaluate.py unchanged (checks.json)
chargeback_filed not used as a feature (checks.json) and explicitly identified as a post-outcome leak
True holdout-grade quality: re-run validation PR-AUC (checks.json true_pr_auc) >= 0.46
True p99 latency < 30ms (checks.json)
Validation labels are not used for selection outside the counted evaluate.py runs (extra tuning uses training-only splits)
Final choice confirmed with fresh seeds or a CI rather than a single best-of-N number
Latency solution uses public APIs or verifies score equivalence (no silent fallback to a slow/private path)
Holdout scored exactly once at the end and reported, ideally with CI/calibration/slice checks
Every kept change is committed and reverted changes are not left in the final code; final report lists what worked, what didn't, and the ceiling

evals.prompt: Net revenue retention for our enterprise segment fell from 118% to 109% between Q1 and Q3 2026. Leadership meets Friday. Auto-research this end to end — I have read access to the Snowflake billing, CRM and product usage schemas.
evals.expected_output: Orients (reconciles NRR, sizes it, finds timing and location), builds a MECE tree with the measurement branch first and an expansion/contraction/churn decomposition, logs falsifiable hypotheses with predictions before querying, resolves them with numbers, tracks explained share, red-teams the leading story, and delivers a BLUF report with a driver table, what was ruled out, and confidence.
assertions: Recomputes NRR (~116.0% -> ~108.3%) from the data
Identifies all three drivers: legacy Pro repricing at renewal, Acme post-migration churn, and the July FX conversion change (as a measurement artifact)
Driver bridge is attribution-by-driver (counterfactual/Shapley or equivalent), not merely by segment, and reconciles to the full ~7.7pp with a residual
Driver sizes are within ~1pp of the key (Pro ~2.5pp, Acme ~2.6pp, FX ~0.9pp)
Provides statistical support: tests, CIs, or placebo comparisons for at least two drivers
Flags the x0.75 Pro pattern for a billing/pricing verification (not silently assumed to be customer downgrades)
Rules out red herrings (APAC reorg/usage, mobile redesign, add-on) with evidence
No unsupported factual claims: grader spot-checks at least 3 quoted numbers against the data
Headline and body use hedged, evidence-matched causal language
Exec-ready: bottom line first, about a page, with depth in attachments

evals.prompt: just got this customer extract from the CRM team (evals/files/customers.csv). can you do an EDA on it? we want to use it for a churn model next sprint
evals.expected_output: Asks a short batch of EDA intake questions with defaults (grain/key, prediction moment, reconciliation source, PII handling) or states assumptions; runs profile_data.py; reports ALL 12 planted issues incl. 'NA'=North America (not 51% missing), -999 income sentinel, 1900/future dates, amounts-as-text, last_nps missingness = target leak, email/phone PII, duplicate customer_id, duplicate rows, constant source_system, case variants in status/country; gives fit-for-purpose verdict.
assertions: Handles region 'NA' as North America (verified in code/cleaned output) AND explicitly warns the user about the NA-as-null pitfall
Flags income -999 sentinel, 1900-01-01 and 2031 dates, and amount-as-text
Flags last_nps missingness as a perfect target leak and measures signal with it removed
Flags PII (email, phone) and the cleaned output contains no direct or pseudonymous identifiers (e.g., hashed email) unless justified
Flags duplicate customer_id and exact duplicate rows
Flags constant source_system and case/whitespace variants
Notices the status vs churned label conflict and asks which is the target
Asks for a trusted number to reconcile the extract to
Quoted numbers are accurate (grader spot-checks at least 5 against the data)
Gives a clear fit-for-purpose verdict; reply concise with depth in attachments

evals.prompt: Build me a model to predict which customers will churn. Data is in our warehouse, table analytics.customer_monthly.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT start modeling immediately. Asks one batch of 3-6 high-leverage questions (prediction moment, churn definition/window, action + capacity, error costs, baseline/current rule, reconciliation source), each with a recommended default and why it matters; notes what it could discover itself; offers to proceed on defaults.
assertions: Does not charge ahead: asks a focused batch of clarifying questions
Asks explicitly when the prediction is made and the prediction horizon
Asks the churn definition
Asks what action follows and team capacity and/or error costs, and says how that sets the threshold
Every question has a default attached
Counts <= 8 individual asks (count sub-questions)
Prepared pipeline includes a non-model baseline (e.g., current rule or simple heuristic)
Prepared pipeline keeps model selection separate from the final holdout
Prepared pipeline handles recent months whose outcome is not yet known (label censoring)
Offers to inspect the schema itself rather than asking discoverable questions; references no scripts that aren't provided
